findings.title: Incomplete support for WebSocket denial responses in all response types
findings.message: The logic for prefixing ASGI message types with 'websocket.' is only added to the base Response class. Other response types that override __call__, such as StreamingResponse and FileResponse, have not been updated. Consequently, using a StreamingResponse or FileResponse as a denial response will result in incorrect ASGI message types (e.g., 'http.response.start' instead of 'websocket.http.response.start'), which will cause a RuntimeError in the WebSocket state machine.
findings.evidence: prefix = "websocket." if scope["type"] == "websocket" else ""

findings.title: Potential AttributeError in WebSocketDenialResponse
findings.message: WebSocketDenialResponse inherits from both httpx.Response and WebSocketDisconnect. Since httpx.Response.__init__ is called first and does not invoke super().__init__, WebSocketDisconnect.__init__ is never executed. This results in instances of WebSocketDenialResponse lacking the 'code' and 'reason' attributes expected of a WebSocketDisconnect exception, which will cause an AttributeError if they are accessed in error handling code.
findings.evidence: class WebSocketDenialResponse(httpx.Response, WebSocketDisconnect):

suggestion.rationale: Adding an __init__ method ensures that the 'code' and 'reason' attributes are initialized, maintaining compatibility with code that catches WebSocketDisconnect and expects these attributes to be present.

findings.title: Inconsistent reason value in WebSocketDisconnect
findings.message: When reject=True, the reason attribute of the raised WebSocketDisconnect is set to None if not provided in the message, whereas when reject=False (or in previous versions), it defaults to an empty string. This inconsistency might break tests that expect a string value for the reason attribute.
findings.evidence: reason=message.get("reason"),

suggestion.rationale: Using an empty string as the default for the reason attribute maintains consistency with the existing behavior and ensures the attribute is always a string.

findings.title: Potential infinite recursion
findings.message: If a server inconsistently reports range support (e.g., fails a range request but includes 'Accept-Ranges: bytes' in a full GET response), this method will enter an infinite recursion loop. It attempts the lazy fetch, fails, falls back to full download, detects range support, and retries the lazy fetch indefinitely.
findings.evidence: return self._get_info_from_wheel(link.url)

suggestion.rationale: Tracking whether a lazy attempt was already made for the current call prevents infinite recursion if the server's range support reporting is inconsistent.

findings.title: Incorrect seek position in ensure_downloaded
findings.message: The loop seeks to the beginning of the entire requested range ('start') for every missing interval, instead of seeking to the start of each specific interval ('range_start'). This causes data corruption in the backing file as subsequent intervals overwrite previous ones at the wrong offset.
findings.evidence: self.seek(start)

suggestion.rationale: The file pointer must be moved to the start of the specific interval being written to ensure data is placed at the correct offset in the backing file.

findings.title: Unclosed ZipFile object
findings.message: A ZipFile object is instantiated without being closed or used in a context manager. While the underlying stream is managed externally, it is better practice to close ZipFile to release internal resources.
findings.evidence: zf = ZipFile(self)

suggestion.rationale: Using a context manager ensures that the ZipFile object is properly closed after use.

findings.title: Use of removed Flask API
findings.message: flask.json.JSONEncoder was removed in Flask 2.3. Modern Flask applications should use the JSONProvider API (app.json) for custom serialization logic. Additionally, the default JSON provider in Flask 2.3+ no longer automatically handles the __html__ protocol, which this test appears to be verifying.
findings.evidence: from flask.json import JSONEncoder

findings.title: Redundant assertion
findings.message: This assertion is redundant as the variable 'encoder' was just instantiated from the JSONEncoder class on the previous line.
findings.evidence: assert isinstance(encoder, JSONEncoder)

suggestion.rationale: Removing redundant assertion to clean up the test code.

findings.title: Inefficient class attribute access
findings.message: TEST_HTML is a class attribute. Accessing it via an instance ObjectWithHTML() is less efficient than accessing it via the class ObjectWithHTML.TEST_HTML.
